Reference paired evaluation, 4 Nov 2026. Task: “I work full-time on weekdays, so I can only do Saturday or Sunday. List Beginner courses that meet on Saturday or Sunday.” The redesigned catalogue keeps every class day and level one click deep, so the agent opened course pages one at a time and answered after 13 requests with 1 of the 4 courses. After the change, the agent read all 4 from the course cards in 3. Screenshot and memory are unedited.

LARKSPUR COMMUNITY COLLEGE · REFERENCE PAIRED EVALUATION, 4 NOV 2026

Looks great to people.
But can AI agents navigate it?

Larkspur Community College had a visually appealing website built around familiar browsing patterns. Course fees, schedules and availability were accessible on individual course pages—a natural design choice for human visitors, but one that created unexpected friction for AI agents.

On the original catalogue, agents answered 0 of 3 questions correctly. Agent Readiness identified the obstacles and recommended targeted improvements. After implementing those changes, agents answered 3 of 3 correctly, using 74% fewer model requests.

Results from our reference paired evaluation. Individual live runs may vary.

AGENT-READY WEBSITE

01 — THE AGENTIC WEB

A page that’s easy for people can be expensive for agents.

A person scans the course catalogue, opens a course or two and books. An agent does the same work one model request at a time: read, decide, navigate. On Larkspur Community College’s freshly redesigned catalogue every fee, class day and seat count sat one click deep, on fourteen separate pages. The agents’ budgets ran out before the work did.

Analytics won’t show you this. The pages load, nothing throws an error, and the agent leaves with a partial answer — or a guess. Agent Readiness shows what analytics can’t: whether the answer was right, which pages the agent saw, where it got stuck, and what it cost.
